properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock comprises Carboniferous Lower Oil-Shale sedimentary strata (sandstones, shales) overlain by glacial till. Structural masonry utilizes local pale-ochre to cream-grey Craigleith and Hailes quartz-arenite carboniferous sandstones, bonded with historical non-hydraulic to weakly hydraulic lime mortar (slaked quicklime and local sharp river sand aggregate). Subterranean drainage flows down towards the nearby Water of Leith valley.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Belgrave Crescent Gardens vegetation belt (late September phenology): Mature canopy dominated by *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm), and *Fraxinus excelsior* (European Ash). Foliage displays early autumn senescence with patchy chlorosis, dull ochre edge-browning, and slight crown thinning. Dense understorey shrubs with dark green fading foliage.

properties.architectural_summary: Left foreground/midground: Victorian three-to-four-storey residential tenement terrace with canted ashlar bay windows, moulded stringcourses, cornice lines, and timber double-hung sash-and-case fenestration. Center midground: Gothic Revival ecclesiastical structure featuring a tall battlemented square bell tower with corner crocketed pinnacles, lancet window apertures, buttressed nave, and pitched slate roof. Right side: Curving street alignment bounded by low ashlar coped retaining walls fronting deep garden tree lines. Planar vertical lines rectified to plumb geometry; mesh deformation flattened to true elevations.
